changes.text: Week → Day: all-day hours are included in the day totals. The Total bar sits under the grid so it no longer covers the last rows.
Week → Day: overlapping entries show Multiple (hover for how to edit). Submitted days show a lock icon instead of the word Locked.
Tasks list Total row stays visible while you scroll.
Stopping and deleting the same stopwatch work item at once no longer returns a 500.
Edits you make in Google Calendar on a Tyme-created event now come back into Tyme.
Tasks no longer overwrites your saved All / Week / Project view if you click a tab before the page finishes loading.
Organizations is its own menu and role (User can view, Editor can create/edit). Archive and delete stay with global Admin.
Details left blank are stored as empty (null), not a placeholder. A project is required when you log time.
After you connect Google Calendar, you choose Export and Import (and the one-time backfill) in that first dialog.
Reports Time by Project and Daily Hours can group by organization or project group and show percent or hours.
App Settings has an Intranet tab. Add User uses a clearer role picker. Scoped admins can see everyone in the user list (changing roles is still limited).
Left/right arrow keys move to the previous/next week on Tasks, or the previous/next page on tables, unless you are typing or a dialog is open.
Installed app icons use an anonymized clock mark (no third-party branding).
Task and stopwatch free-text field is Details (not Name) end-to-end: API, UI, and database schema for greenfield installs.
Managers can submit time on behalf of eligible team members when workspace setting allows it.
Project-first task entry with optional Details; Task Details field component and week/day grids use the same rules.
Google Calendar pull/disconnect improvements and webhook-based import worker for missed events.
Organization archive/activate cluster rules and organization name picker filters.
Calendar OAuth uses the signed-in user's domain (no hard-coded hosted domain).
Provision and auth domain messaging stay multi-tenant and brand-neutral.
Removed pricing, dollar amounts, and cost-lever guidance from self-host documentation. Operational notes about serverless auto-pause and cold starts remain without commercial framing.
Tasks list pages through full history (no 10,000-row cap).
Week view supports multiple in-progress draft rows at once.
Google Calendar disconnect/reconnect; Pull missed events checks every [tag] in an event title.
App version at the bottom of the left nav, with a "New" badge when a new version is first seen.
Versions page listing release notes (linked from the nav version).
Editor:Tyme role: create and edit projects, without sharing availability with team (Manager+).
Submit page: early submission for the current (or future) month when time is already entered.
Duration storage limits enforced consistently across manual entry and timer completion.
Reports page has a dedicated filter row.
Stopwatch sessions UX, project autocomplete (infinite scroll / open upward), work-item lock when any session is submitted.
Task list column alignment; all-day duration uses a tooltip instead of a conflicting icon.
Sidebar stray horizontal scrollbar next to the version number.
Quieted noisy EF Core SQL command logging in the Function worker.
Removed the SQL keepalive timer that blocked serverless database auto-pause.
Changelog process documented for developers; CI can gate version bumps on changelog entries.
Tasks All / Week / Project views with week entry grids and duration UX.
User default start time (08:00) and workspace TymeTrackTimeOfDay setting.
Stopwatch session create-duration flow and browser Tasks page preferences.
Time of day parsing for bare hour+meridiem (e.g. 9P) and HH:mm:ss under any culture.
Initial public My.Workspace product baseline.
